summary:
ASTRA – Astronaut Self-monitoring, Telemetry & Risk Assessment

ASTRA is an offline-first health decision-support system designed for astronauts on long-duration missions where communication delays make real-time medical oversight impossible. During a 180-day mission, the system continuously monitors 17 physiological and behavioral indicators — including heart rate variability, SpO₂, grip strength, sleep, radiation dose, and mood — against each astronaut's own personal baseline, not generic population norms.

It uses exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) drift detection, z-score deviation bands, persistence filters, and a transparent rules layer to flag emerging health trends early — before any single metric crosses a hard threshold. When a pattern is detected, it explains why in plain language and recommends tiered actions (Tier 1 self-care through Tier 3 ground escalation with a one-tap downlink report).

In evaluation across 20 simulated mission runs, ASTRA detected infection within 4 days, CO₂ habitat events within 1 day, and all solar particle events instantly — with fewer than 0.7 false alarms per 30 days. The system works fully offline via a service worker with on-device IndexedDB storage, with no machine learning model required, making every decision auditable and explainable by the astronaut and flight surgeon alike.
details:
ASTRA – Astronaut Self-monitoring, Telemetry & Risk Assessment

What It Does and How It Works

ASTRA is a web-based clinical decision support system (CDSS) built for astronauts on long-duration missions — particularly deep-space or lunar missions where the communication delay with Earth makes real-time medical oversight impractical or impossible.

The system continuously monitors 17 physiological and behavioral indicators organized across six health domains:

  • Immune — resting temperature, fatigue, hydration
  • Cardiovascular — resting heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), SpO₂, systolic and diastolic blood pressure
  • Bone & Muscle — daily exercise minutes, grip strength, nutrition score
  • Mind & Mood — sleep hours, mood, stress, headache severity
  • Habitat Air — cabin CO₂ partial pressure
  • Radiation — daily radiation dose and cumulative mission dose (mSv)

Rather than comparing an astronaut's readings against population-level clinical limits (which are designed for Earth patients), ASTRA builds a personal baseline for each crew member during mission days 8–30. Every subsequent reading is evaluated in terms of how far it has drifted from that individual's own normal. This matters because what is normal for one astronaut may be abnormal for another — and population thresholds completely miss the early, subtle shift that is most actionable.

The core detection pipeline is:

  1. Z-score standardization against the personal baseline mean and standard deviation.
  2. Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) smoothing with λ = 0.3, which weights recent readings more heavily while filtering daily noise.
  3. Persistence filter — a level must hold for at least 2 consecutive days before it is counted, eliminating one-day spikes.
  4. Rules layer — cross-domain synergy patterns that no single metric can catch: an Infection Pattern fires when temperature is elevated alongside fatigue, elevated heart rate, or poor sleep; a Habitat Pattern fires when elevated CO₂ coincides with worse mood, sleep, or stress — distinguishing environmental causes from true illness.
  5. Linear drift forecasting — projects which indicator will reach the Watch threshold first based on its current 5-day slope, warning the astronaut before an alert fires.
  6. Tiered escalation — outputs Tier 0 (normal), Tier 1 (self-manage), Tier 2 (crew medical officer), or Tier 3 (ground contact required), with specific actionable guidance at each tier — none of which include medication doses.

The system also detects solar particle events in real time (daily dose > 5 mSv), immediately escalates the radiation domain to Act, tightens immune detection thresholds for the following 14 days (since SPE exposure degrades immune function), and displays a persistent banner.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The core problem ASTRA addresses is the asymmetry of information and time during deep-space missions. A Mars mission involves a 20-minute one-way communication delay. An astronaut experiencing the onset of an infection, cardiovascular irregularity, or psychological decline cannot wait 40+ minutes for a ground response. ASTRA puts a capable, explainable triage system directly in the astronaut's hands — onboard, offline, with no dependency on ground connectivity.

Key benefits:

  • Early detection — evaluation across 20 simulated missions shows infection detected in a median of 4 days, CO₂ events in 1 day, solar particle events in 0 days (instantly), and bone/muscle decline in 3 days.
  • Low false alarm rate — 0.66 false alarms per 30 days on healthy-only missions, below the threshold of alert fatigue.
  • Fully explainable — every alert includes the contributing indicators, their values vs the astronaut's own baseline, and the reason in plain language. There is no black-box model. A flight surgeon can audit every decision.
  • Offline-first — the entire clinical intelligence engine runs in the browser with no backend required. All astronaut data is stored on-device in IndexedDB. The service worker caches the full app shell on first load, so it operates indefinitely without network access.
  • Ground summary — a single button generates a plain-text telemetry summary with the last 14 days of vital trends, cumulative radiation dose, and escalation tier — ready to copy into a store-and-forward ground uplink.

Technologies Used

Layer

Technology

Frontend

Vanilla JavaScript (ES Modules), HTML5, CSS3

Clinical Engine

Pure JS — z-score, EWMA drift, persistence, linear forecasting (engine.js)

Offline Storage

Browser IndexedDB via native API (db.js)

Offline Availability

Service Worker (Cache API, app-shell pattern)

Backend (optional)

Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy (async), Pydantic, SQLite / PostgreSQL

Node.js Server

Node.js 20 — static file server + /api/v1 ground bridge with RFC 7233 byte-range streaming (server.mjs)

Data Simulation

Python (simulator/simulate.py) with scripted mission anomalies for ground truth evaluation

Testing

Node.js built-in test runner, 16 unit tests covering detection, validation, and range logic

Containerization

Docker (Alpine Node 20 image + Python 3.11 slim image, docker-compose.yml)

Deployment configs

Render, Railway, Fly.io, Vercel, Netlify, systemd (Linux VPS)

CI/CD

GitHub Actions

Research Integration

NASA HRP Hazards, NASA HRP Risks, NASA HRP Research, CSA Radiation Monitoring, CSA Space Science

Deliberately, no machine learning model was used. There is no labeled spaceflight health dataset suitable for training a clinical model. ML outputs are not natively explainable, and explainability is non-negotiable in a medical decision support context. The statistical approach used by ASTRA is auditable, predictable, and can be reviewed and tuned by a flight surgeon without touching any code — all thresholds and action text live in a single configuration file (web/config.js).

Creativity and Design Decisions

  • Personal baselines, not population norms. The choice to treat each astronaut as their own control group is the defining design decision. It means ASTRA catches subtle personal drift that universal clinical limits entirely miss.
  • Domain synergy rules. The Infection Pattern and Habitat Pattern rules reflect a real clinical insight: in a closed habitat, elevated CO₂ mimics illness symptoms. A system that only monitors vital signs without environmental context would systematically misclassify CO₂ events as individual health issues. ASTRA separates the two.
  • Post-SPE immune tightening. Following a solar particle event, immune thresholds automatically tighten by 25% for 14 days, reflecting NASA's documented finding that radiation exposure suppresses immune function and increases infection risk — a cross-domain interaction no simple alert system would model.
  • Offline-first by constraint. ASTRA was designed to work without ground contact, not just as a fallback. All data lives on the device, all intelligence runs in the browser, and the backend is a progressive enhancement — not a dependency.
  • Safety and ethics by design. No medication doses are suggested anywhere in the application. The system explicitly labels itself as decision support, not diagnosis. Data never leaves the device unless the astronaut initiates a ground summary copy. Tier 3 always escalates to a human.
